lessons.name: eCential Robotics
lessons.summary: eCential Robotics builds a surgical platform that combines imaging, navigation, and robotic assistance for bone surgery.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

eCential Robotics builds a surgical platform that combines imaging, navigation, and robotic assistance for bone surgery.

![eCential surgical imaging and robotic platform](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-ecential-robotics.webp)
*eCential surgical imaging and robotic platform. Source: [Official site](https://www.ecential-robotics.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Three linked functions:** imaging shows anatomy, navigation tracks instruments relative to it, and robotic assistance helps guide the surgical workflow.
- **The eCential integrated surgical platform** brings these functions together rather than asking the team to operate disconnected systems.
- **Open architecture** lets industrial partners develop surgical applications; that does not mean the software is open source.

> **Key idea:** A unified interface is valuable only if images, tracked tools, and physical motion agree.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think plugin platform:** partner applications resemble software extensions sharing a common runtime, but physical accuracy and clinical validation remain essential.
- **A concrete example:** compare the two-dimensional image, three-dimensional reconstruction, and tracked tool position; they describe different views of the same surgical scene.
- **A useful study topic:** trace how a coordinate error could propagate from an image into a tool-guidance display.

## How to engage

1. **Start with the overview** and identify which components sense, compute, and move before reading clinical application descriptions.
2. **Use public contact channels** to propose a student talk about calibration or integration, not access to patients or surgical equipment.
3. **Prepare a simulation-only question:** show a coordinate-frame demo and ask what additional evidence a medical workflow would require.

lessons.name: Eclore Actuators
lessons.summary: Eclore Actuators folds polymers into compact protective bellows and robot protection kits, bringing origami-like geometry into industrial robotics.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Eclore Actuators folds polymers into compact protective bellows and robot protection kits, bringing origami-like geometry into industrial robotics.

![Eclore protective bellows fitted to a SCARA robot](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-eclore-actuators.webp)
*Eclore protective bellows fitted to a SCARA robot. Source: [Official site](https://www.eclore-actuators.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **A bellows** is a folded sleeve that expands and contracts while shielding a moving part from dust, liquids, or debris.
- **SCARA protection kits** fit a class of industrial arm commonly used for fast assembly and handling; Eclore offers robot-specific fittings.
- **Geometry does useful work:** the folds allow motion without requiring a large rigid enclosure around the moving axis.

> **Key idea:** Mechanical packaging can determine whether a robot keeps working outside a clean demonstration.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think protective wrapper:** like validating input around an API, a mechanical sleeve protects a vulnerable component without replacing its core function.
- **A concrete comparison:** inspect the same bellows compressed and extended; check that its travel accommodates the robot axis at both extremes.
- **Hardware matters for software:** a successful motion command is not enough if contamination gradually damages the mechanism.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the product clips** to distinguish passive protection from powered actuation; the company name alone does not establish what a product does.
2. **Read the technology page** and list material, travel, and environmental constraints for a hypothetical student mechanism.
3. **Contact the public engineering team** with a dimensioned sketch and one materials question, rather than assuming a standard sleeve fits every arm.

lessons.name: Ecorobotix
lessons.summary: Ecorobotix builds AI-guided precision sprayers that identify plants and apply treatment selectively instead of spraying an entire field uniformly.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Ecorobotix builds AI-guided precision sprayers that identify plants and apply treatment selectively instead of spraying an entire field uniformly.

![Ecorobotix precision spraying equipment in a field](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-ecorobotix.webp)
*Ecorobotix precision spraying equipment in a field. Source: [Official site](https://ecorobotix.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The ARA620 UHP Sprayer** is a tractor-mounted implement; do not confuse precision spraying with a fully autonomous tractor.
- **Plant-by-Plant AI** distinguishes crops and weeds so treatment can target particular plants rather than the surrounding soil.
- **A camera-to-action problem:** the useful output is not just a plant label, but treatment at the correct physical location.

> **Key idea:** Plant recognition becomes useful only when a physical treatment reaches the intended plant.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think conditional execution:** a detector supplies the condition, but the nozzle must execute the action at the right place and time.
- **A concrete example:** compare a carrot and a weed in one image, then mark which plant should receive the selected treatment.
- **A software-friendly study:** prototype image annotation and measure missed weeds separately from crop misclassification; those errors have different consequences.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official field footage** to identify the tractor, camera area, and spraying implement before studying the AI description.
2. **Read the carrot application** and write down how a crop-specific model changes the classification task.
3. **Use the public contact route** for a technical discussion about vision evaluation; propose image analysis, not student chemical spraying.

lessons.name: Effidence
lessons.summary: Effidence builds mobile robots and navigation software that move materials through industrial sites and warehouses.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Effidence builds mobile robots and navigation software that move materials through industrial sites and warehouses.

![EffiBOT following a worker during order preparation](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-effidence.webp)
*EffiBOT following a worker during order preparation. Source: [Official site](https://www.effidence.com/effibot-2/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **EffiBOT** is a wheeled material-handling robot that can follow a worker or transport parts autonomously.
- **Different operating modes** address different workflows: following a person during order preparation is not the same task as an unattended delivery.
- **Navigation and coordination** connect individual robot movement to the wider flow of materials around a site.

> **Key idea:** A mobile robot is valuable when its navigation fits the material flow, not merely when it can drive.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think delivery service:** a mission resembles a queued job, while navigation handles the physical route needed to complete it.
- **A concrete example:** compare following an order picker with delivering parts between two workstations; identify who chooses the destination in each case.
- **Integration is the lesson:** the same mobile base can need different attachments, mission rules, and interfaces in different factories.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the application video** and draw the boundary between the worker, mobile base, and material-handling attachment.
2. **Read the navigation page** before proposing a simulation of two delivery destinations with an obstacle between them.
3. **Send a focused public enquiry** about mission scheduling or indoor/outdoor transitions, including a small demo and its measured failure cases.

lessons.name: Embodied AI
lessons.summary: Embodied AI is a Lausanne company combining compliant robots, human demonstrations, and on-site learning for repetitive physical work.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Embodied AI is a Lausanne company combining compliant robots, human demonstrations, and on-site learning for repetitive physical work.

![Embodied AI AIR01 wheeled humanoid](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-embodied-ai.webp)
*Embodied AI AIR01 wheeled humanoid. Source: [Official site](https://embodiedai.ch/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **AIR (Embodied AI)** is its wheeled humanoid; the company also presents two-arm workcells for tasks that do not need a mobile body.
- **Imitation learning** means learning actions from demonstrations; teleoperation means a human remotely guides the robot to produce those examples.
- **Human supervision** remains part of its deployment story: people can guide the system and intervene when necessary.

> **Key idea:** The right embodiment follows the task; not every manipulation problem requires a humanoid.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think iterative deployment:** observe a workflow, collect examples, and improve behavior using feedback from the actual operating environment.
- **A concrete example:** study the cable-handling demonstration and separate seeing a connector, approaching it, and making physical contact.
- **A useful comparison:** the same software stack can serve a mobile humanoid or fixed arms; start with the task before choosing the body.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official task clips** and list which actions are visible versus which autonomy claims require additional evidence.
2. **Read the launch coverage** alongside the product page to distinguish announced intentions from demonstrated behavior.
3. **Use the public contact form** to propose a student discussion about demonstration quality, reporting your own task, dataset, and evaluation limits.

lessons.name: Embotech
lessons.summary: Embotech develops autonomous driving systems for controlled industrial environments such as factories, logistics yards, and ports.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Embotech develops autonomous driving systems for controlled industrial environments such as factories, logistics yards, and ports.

![Embotech autonomous terminal tractor](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-embotech.webp)
*Embotech autonomous terminal tractor. Source: [Official site](https://www.embotech.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Two concrete applications:** autonomous terminal tractors move trailers, while automated vehicle marshalling moves cars through automotive facilities.
- **Motion planning** selects a feasible route and movement; control turns that plan into steering and speed commands.
- **Separate safety architecture:** the company describes AI-enabled decisions alongside a deterministic safety layer, rather than treating learned behavior as sufficient assurance.

> **Key idea:** Industrial autonomy combines useful motion with clearly bounded operating and safety assumptions.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think scheduler plus guardrails:** optimize the requested movement, but keep an independent path for enforcing operating constraints.
- **A concrete comparison:** draw a car moving between factory stations and a tractor moving a container; list their different turning-space requirements.
- **Related map node Exwayz** supplies a useful comparison: localization estimates position, while a complete driving system must also choose and execute actions.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official driving footage** before reading the application pages; identify the vehicle, operating area, and surrounding traffic.
2. **Study the technology description** and separate performance claims from the stated safety architecture.
3. **Contact the public team** with a simulation of one constrained route and a precise question about planning or validation, not a request for vehicle access.

lessons.name: Emovo Care
lessons.summary: Emovo Care builds wearable robotic hand devices for assisted grasping and research into human movement and interaction.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Emovo Care builds wearable robotic hand devices for assisted grasping and research into human movement and interaction.

![Emovo robotic hand exoskeleton](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-emovo-care.webp)
*Emovo robotic hand exoskeleton. Source: [Official site](https://www.emovocare.com/emovo-clinic), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **An exoskeleton** is a mechanism worn outside the body that assists movement; this one helps fingers open and close.
- **Emovo Clinic** is presented as a medical device, while **Emovo Research** is explicitly research-only and offers configurable sensing and software interfaces.
- **Control and telemetry** are separate interfaces: commands request movement, while measurements report position, force, or device status.

> **Key idea:** A wearable robot connects software commands to a person, making the intended use and interface limits inseparable.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think hardware API:** a function call changes a real finger mechanism, so input validation and force limits matter beyond ordinary software correctness.
- **A concrete interface example:** the research page describes position commands from 0 to 100 percent; this normalized value is not an angle in degrees.
- **Two different purposes:** studying an interface or recorded signal does not demonstrate a clinical treatment benefit.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the research demonstration** to identify the wearable mechanism and the virtual-reality interaction it supports.
2. **Read the research configuration page** and sketch a mock API client that logs commands separately from returned measurements, without connecting hardware.
3. **Use the public enquiry route** to request research documentation; keep any student proposal non-clinical and do not test assistance on people.

lessons.name: Enchanted Tools
lessons.summary: Enchanted Tools develops expressive Mirokaï service robots designed to move, handle objects, and interact with people in shared spaces.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Enchanted Tools develops expressive Mirokaï service robots designed to move, handle objects, and interact with people in shared spaces.

![Mirokaï robot from Enchanted Tools](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-enchanted-tools.webp)
*Mirokaï robot from Enchanted Tools. Source: [Official site](https://enchanted.tools/robot), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Miroki / Miroka** make appearance part of the interface, rather than hiding the machine behind an industrial enclosure.
- **Social interaction** includes conversation and engagement; the robot page also describes navigation, perception, and assisted object handling.
- **The Mather pilot** explored interactions with residents and staff in a senior-living community, not just a staged exhibition demonstration.

> **Key idea:** A social robot must coordinate a usable conversation with a readable physical presence.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think embodied user interface:** spoken responses, gaze, appearance, and physical movement all affect how a person interprets the system.
- **A concrete example:** compare a robot answering one resident with supporting a group conversation; success requires more than producing a fluent sentence.
- **Evaluation needs context:** the company study page emphasizes sustained interaction, so distinguish initial novelty from continued usefulness.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the VivaTech footage** and annotate one interaction: who initiates it, how the robot responds, and how it ends.
2. **Read the Mather study overview** before proposing an interaction project; write observable measures rather than claiming reduced loneliness from a demo.
3. **Join the public community** through the official site or send a focused enquiry about interaction design, without assuming access to care facilities.

lessons.name: Exotec
lessons.summary: Exotec builds warehouse automation combining Skypod robots, storage infrastructure, and software that coordinates the movement of goods.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Exotec builds warehouse automation combining Skypod robots, storage infrastructure, and software that coordinates the movement of goods.

![Exotec Skypod warehouse robot](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-exotec.webp)
*Exotec Skypod warehouse robot. Source: [Official site](https://www.exotec.com/skypod-automated-storage-retrieval-system/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Skypod** belongs to an automated storage and retrieval system: goods move between storage and workstations rather than workers walking every aisle.
- **Deepsky** is the orchestration layer connecting warehouse management to the automation equipment and its operational state.
- **System integration** matters alongside the robot: picking, buffering, replenishment, and outbound flow must work together.

> **Key idea:** Warehouse automation is a coordinated flow of goods and information, not a collection of fast robots.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think distributed job execution:** an order becomes work assigned across physical machines, with shared inventory state instead of independent scripts.
- **A concrete example:** follow one bin from storage to a picking station, then distinguish the robot trip from the inventory update.
- **A useful student exercise:** simulate two orders competing for one workstation and compare queue policies before adding more robots.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the Skypod demonstration** and label the moving robot, rack, container, and human workstation.
2. **Read the Deepsky overview** to identify which decisions belong to orchestration rather than onboard motion control.
3. **Follow public events** or enquire about an educational talk; Exotours require an invitation, so do not assume student access to customer warehouses.

lessons.name: Exwayz
lessons.summary: Exwayz develops LiDAR mapping, localization, and perception software that helps robots understand where they are in three-dimensional environments.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Exwayz develops LiDAR mapping, localization, and perception software that helps robots understand where they are in three-dimensional environments.

![Exwayz LiDAR view of an urban environment](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-exwayz.webp)
*Exwayz LiDAR view of an urban environment. Source: [Official site](https://exwayz.fr), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Exwayz Engine** processes LiDAR, a sensor that measures distances using laser light, to build maps and estimate position.
- **Localization** finds the sensor inside an existing map; mapping builds that reference from recorded measurements.
- **Point clouds** are collections of measured three-dimensional points, not photographs; the software uses their geometry to recognize places.

> **Key idea:** Knowing where the robot is and deciding what it should do are different software responsibilities.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think spatial lookup:** a robot matches its latest measurements against a stored reference, then passes the estimated pose to other software.
- **A concrete example:** the Embotech case study places Exwayz inside port automation; localization supports driving but does not itself choose a safe route.
- **Useful software skills:** timestamps, coordinate frames, and data interfaces determine whether a correct estimate reaches the robot in a usable form.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the embedded LiDAR clip** and distinguish raw geometry from the estimated path through it.
2. **Read the SDK overview** to identify inputs, outputs, and integration options before proposing a small recorded-data experiment.
3. **Use the public demo channel** with a clearly described dataset and evaluation question; do not assume proprietary software is freely downloadable.

lessons.name: FERNRIDE
lessons.summary: FERNRIDE combines autonomous driving and remote human assistance to move cargo in industrial yards and container terminals.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

FERNRIDE combines autonomous driving and remote human assistance to move cargo in industrial yards and container terminals.

![FERNRIDE industrial transport vehicle](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-fernride.webp)
*FERNRIDE industrial transport vehicle. Source: [Official site](https://www.fernride.com), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Human-assisted autonomy** lets vehicles drive themselves while remote operators help with situations the system cannot resolve alone.
- **Sensors and compute** combine cameras, radar, and LiDAR distance measurements with planning and vehicle control.
- **The FERNRIDE Gen 4 vehicle kit** is the related map entry; the platform page describes the broader autonomy, safety, and fleet-management stack.

> **Key idea:** A practical autonomy system needs a defined response when automation reaches its limits.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think service escalation:** an automated process handles routine work while exceptional cases reach a human, rather than silently guessing.
- **A concrete example:** moving a container requires both following a route and coordinating with terminal operations; vehicle intelligence alone is insufficient.
- **A useful evaluation question:** measure when remote assistance is requested, how it is resolved, and whether the vehicle returns to autonomous operation.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the company overview** and identify the truck, operating area, and remote assistance role.
2. **Read the terminal application page** alongside the platform description to separate a customer workflow from individual technical components.
3. **Use public events or contact channels** to propose a talk on exception handling and fleet software, supported by a simulation rather than vehicle experiments.

lessons.name: FieldAI
lessons.summary: FieldAI builds general-purpose autonomy software intended to let different robot bodies operate in unfamiliar, unstructured environments.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

FieldAI builds general-purpose autonomy software intended to let different robot bodies operate in unfamiliar, unstructured environments.

![Different robot platforms presented by FieldAI](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-fieldai.webp)
*Different robot platforms presented by FieldAI. Source: [Official site](https://www.fieldai.com), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Field Foundation Models (FieldAI)** combine learned behavior with physics-based reasoning and explicit estimates of uncertainty.
- **Unstructured environments** are places whose layout or conditions are not fully controlled, such as an active construction site.
- **Different bodies, shared autonomy:** the company presents its software across robot shapes rather than selling one fixed robot design.

> **Key idea:** Reusable autonomy must account for both the robot body and uncertainty in the environment.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think portable runtime:** one software approach targets different hardware, but each robot still has its own movement and sensing constraints.
- **A concrete example:** construction monitoring pairs robot travel with collecting site information; reaching a destination and producing useful inspection data are separate outcomes.
- **Uncertainty matters:** a system should represent what it cannot confidently infer, not just output a route with no indication of doubt.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the field footage** and list visible terrain, robot types, and surrounding people before accepting broad generalization claims.
2. **Read the technology overview** and distinguish what the company explains publicly from model details it does not release.
3. **Use the public contact route** to propose a student session on evaluating field autonomy, bringing a small benchmark with clear failure cases.

lessons.name: Figure
lessons.summary: Figure builds humanoid robots and the Helix AI system that connects visual observations and instructions to physical actions.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Figure builds humanoid robots and the Helix AI system that connects visual observations and instructions to physical actions.

![Figure 03 humanoid robot](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-figure.webp)
*Figure 03 humanoid robot. Source: [Official site](https://www.figure.ai/figure), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Figure 03** is a human-shaped robot with arms, hands, and legs; its body is designed for spaces and objects used by people.
- **Helix (Figure)** is the related AI system, not another robot body; vision, language, and action connect seeing, understanding instructions, and moving.
- **Two connected challenges:** recognizing an object is different from controlling fingers and balance while interacting with it.

> **Key idea:** A humanoid demonstration combines perception, learned decisions, and physical control; inspect those layers separately.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think model plus hardware backend:** the policy selects actions, but motors and sensors determine what those actions physically achieve.
- **A concrete example:** in a household manipulation demonstration, separate identifying an item, reaching it, closing the hand, and placing it.
- **A useful study target:** compare task completion with recovery after an object moves; a successful clip does not establish reliability across unseen homes.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the Figure 03 introduction** and label which features belong to the body versus the learned control system.
2. **Read the Helix overview** and annotate the observations and commands involved in one demonstrated task.
3. **Follow official technical updates** or propose a focused student discussion through public channels; do not assume access to robot hardware or model weights.

lessons.name: Fixposition
lessons.summary: Fixposition combines satellite positioning, cameras, and inertial sensors to estimate robot position when satellite signals become unreliable.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Fixposition combines satellite positioning, cameras, and inertial sensors to estimate robot position when satellite signals become unreliable.

![Fixposition positioning sensor hardware](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-fixposition.webp)
*Fixposition positioning sensor hardware. Source: [Official site](https://www.fixposition.com/pages/our-product), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Sensor fusion** combines complementary measurements rather than trusting one sensor in every situation.
- **GNSS** means satellite navigation; **RTK** uses correction data to improve its accuracy, but buildings and trees can still disrupt reception.
- **Vision-RTK 2** packages cameras, satellite reception, and inertial sensing; the company also offers xFusion technology for integration into other hardware.

> **Key idea:** Reliable positioning uses complementary evidence and exposes its limitations to the rest of the robot.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think fault-tolerant inputs:** cameras and motion measurements help bridge weak satellite reception, but a positioning estimate still has uncertainty.
- **A concrete example:** sketch a robot moving from an open field into a barn; mark which measurements remain informative as satellite visibility changes.
- **Integration is software work:** message timestamps, coordinate conventions, and diagnostic status matter as much as reading a position value.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the positioning demonstration** and notice the transitions between open and obstructed environments.
2. **Read the integration manual** and inspect the public ROS driver, which connects sensor messages to a common robotics software framework.
3. **Begin with recorded messages** or a mock receiver and propose a technical discussion through public support channels; hardware purchase is not necessary to study interfaces.

resources.title: Sensor fusion-based positioning for autonomous platforms | Vision-RTK 2

lessons.name: Flexion Robotics
lessons.summary: Flexion Robotics develops AI control software for humanoids, using simulation and learning to connect physical skills with longer tasks.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Flexion Robotics develops AI control software for humanoids, using simulation and learning to connect physical skills with longer tasks.

![Humanoid robotics development presented by Flexion](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-flexion-robotics.webp)
*Humanoid robotics development presented by Flexion. Source: [Official site](https://flexion.ai), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Reinforcement learning** improves behavior through trial and feedback; simulation allows those trials without repeatedly risking physical hardware.
- **Reflect** is the company’s approach to longer autonomous tasks, connecting higher-level decisions with learned movement capabilities.
- **Cross-body deployment** is a stated goal: the software is intended for different humanoid platforms rather than only one robot model.

> **Key idea:** Long tasks require reliable transitions and recovery between skills, not only impressive individual movements.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think orchestrator plus functions:** a longer task selects and combines lower-level skills, but physical outcomes are less predictable than ordinary function returns.
- **A concrete example:** a delivery mission includes approaching a door, passing through it, and carrying an item; errors can accumulate between those stages.
- **Evaluation should include recovery:** completing one sequence once is different from handling a blocked doorway or an object in an unexpected position.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the Reflect mission** and list the distinct decisions required before reading the technical explanation.
2. **Compare the Reflect releases** to identify what changed in task length, observations, and autonomy rather than treating every demo as a new robot.
3. **Use the public contact route** to propose a student discussion about simulated evaluation, sharing a reproducible task and failure analysis rather than requesting private models.

lessons.name: Flink Robotics
lessons.summary: Flink Robotics develops mobile robotic handling systems that adapt to logistics tasks such as separating, picking, and moving parcels.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Flink Robotics develops mobile robotic handling systems that adapt to logistics tasks such as separating, picking, and moving parcels.

![Flinkbot gripper lifting a parcel](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-flink-robotics.webp)
*Flinkbot gripper lifting a parcel. Source: [Official site](https://www.flink.so/technology), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Flinkbot** and **Flinkbot mini** are the linked robot platforms; the company presents them as adaptable systems rather than fixed conveyor installations.
- **Singulation** means separating mixed items so they can enter the next handling stage one by one.
- **Perception and gripping** combine cameras, force information, and robot state with task-specific grippers; the technology page also describes vacuum handling.

> **Key idea:** Handling varied parcels requires adapting the interaction, not just recognizing the item.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think feedback-driven workflow:** detect an item, choose a grasp, move it, and update the scene rather than replaying the same coordinates blindly.
- **A concrete example:** a soft mailer and rigid box may need different contact and suction behavior even when both count as one parcel.
- **World models** represent how the scene may change; a useful model must account for contact and movement, not merely label objects.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the technology clips** and identify where sensing changes the next action during a parcel-handling attempt.
2. **Compare product and application pages** to separate robot features from assumptions about the surrounding logistics process.
3. **Use the official contact channel** to propose a manipulation-learning talk, bringing a small recorded grasp experiment and a clearly bounded question about failures.

lessons.name: Flyability
lessons.summary: Flyability builds collision-tolerant drones and inspection software for gathering visual and spatial data inside confined industrial spaces.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Flyability builds collision-tolerant drones and inspection software for gathering visual and spatial data inside confined industrial spaces.

![Flyability Elios 3 drone inside its protective cage](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-flyability.webp)
*Flyability Elios 3 drone inside its protective cage. Source: [Official site](https://www.flyability.com/elios-3), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Elios 3** flies inside a protective cage, allowing contact with its surroundings during inspection rather than requiring a completely obstacle-free flight.
- **SLAM** means simultaneous localization and mapping: estimating movement while building a map when satellite positioning is unavailable.
- **Inspection payloads** are carried instruments; the platform supports different measurement tasks, while Inspector software organizes and analyzes the collected data.

> **Key idea:** An inspection robot succeeds when it returns interpretable, located evidence, not simply when it flies.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think crawler plus indexed database:** the drone gathers evidence, but useful inspection also requires locating and retrieving each observation afterward.
- **A concrete example:** an image of a crack is more useful when linked to its location inside a three-dimensional model of the asset.
- **Two different objectives:** keeping the drone stable is not the same as capturing enough evidence for a human inspector to assess equipment.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the mine inspection** and identify why confined geometry changes the sensing and flight problem.
2. **Explore Inspector and training information** to understand the data workflow; the training simulator is offered to Elios 3 users, not as an unrestricted student download.
3. **Use public webinars or contact channels** for an inspection-engineering discussion; keep student experiments in simulation rather than entering hazardous industrial spaces.

lessons.name: Fotokite
lessons.summary: Fotokite builds actively tethered drones that give emergency responders continuous elevated thermal and color camera views.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Fotokite builds actively tethered drones that give emergency responders continuous elevated thermal and color camera views.

![Fotokite Sigma transport-case system](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-fotokite.webp)
*Fotokite Sigma transport-case system. Source: [Official site](https://fotokite.com/transport-case/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Fotokite Sigma** connects the aircraft to its ground station through a tether carrying power and data, rather than relying only on an onboard battery.
- **Active tethering** is part of flight control; the system automates launch, flight, and landing instead of requiring continuous manual piloting.
- **Two configurations:** a transport case moves between vehicles, while a rooftop box integrates the system into a response vehicle.

> **Key idea:** A tether can exchange free flight range for persistent power, data, and simpler operation.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think persistent sensor service:** the aircraft supplies a live viewpoint while responders focus on interpreting the scene and coordinating their work.
- **A concrete example:** thermal imagery helps responders examine roof hot spots while a color view provides visual context; the two streams answer different questions.
- **A design tradeoff:** the tether enables sustained observation but bounds where the aircraft can operate relative to its ground station.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the deployment footage** and identify the ground station, tether, aircraft, and displayed camera views.
2. **Compare the case and rooftop pages** to understand how packaging changes deployment without changing the basic sensing purpose.
3. **Use the public contact route** for a student session on sensor streaming or interface design; study recorded imagery rather than deploying near emergency operations.

lessons.name: Fourier
lessons.summary: Fourier develops rehabilitation robots and humanoid platforms, connecting assisted human movement with whole-body robotics and interaction.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Fourier develops rehabilitation robots and humanoid platforms, connecting assisted human movement with whole-body robotics and interaction.

![Fourier GR-3 humanoid robot](/img/lessons/orgs_startup_2-fourier.webp)
*Fourier GR-3 humanoid robot. Source: [Official site](https://www.fftai.com/en/grx/gr3), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Two product families:** rehabilitation devices support movement therapy, while GR-series humanoids combine legs, arms, hands, and interactive sensing.
- **GR-3** uses vision, audio, and tactile feedback; tactile sensing measures physical contact rather than inferring everything from camera images.
- **RehabHub** brings different therapy systems and their data into a connected clinical workflow; it is not the name of one humanoid.

> **Key idea:** Similar robotics components can serve very different human-facing purposes and validation requirements.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think platform plus applications:** shared engineering capabilities support different products, but a rehabilitation device and general-purpose humanoid have different intended uses.
- **A concrete example:** compare measuring a patient’s assisted arm movement with detecting a touch on a humanoid’s torso; both need sensing, but different evaluation.
- **The map also links Fourier Max (Meta humanoid):** treat that entry as a separate collaboration topic, not as another name for the public GR-3 product.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the GR-3 exhibition footage** to identify visible movement and interaction rather than extrapolating clinical benefits.
2. **Read the product and company pages** to distinguish rehabilitation systems, humanoids, and research ecosystem resources.
3. **Use public developer or contact channels** to request an educational discussion about sensing and control; keep any student proposal non-clinical and simulation-based.
